security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, scientific taxonomy examples, and benign ETE documentation. Confirmed risks are limited to automatic creation of a hidden taxonomy cache in the user home directory and sudo-based package installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Automatic hidden NCBI taxonomy cache in the home directory
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before first NCBITaxa use, document the exact cache path and size, and suggest an explicit dbfile path when possible.
Replace sudo commands with a warning that elevated package installation requires user approval, and provide non-privileged alternatives where available.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic tree work often requires many ETE APIs, file formats, and taxonomy steps. This skill gives Claude guided workflows for tree analysis, NCBI taxonomy, and publication-quality visualization.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to read, write, prune, root, and compare trees in Newick and related formats.
Guides PhyloTree workflows for evolutionary event detection, orthology, and paralogy analysis.
Shows how to use NCBITaxa for taxid translation, lineage retrieval, and taxonomy-based trees.
Provides visualization patterns for PDF, SVG, PNG, circular trees, node styles, and faces.
Includes command-line helper scripts for tree operations and quick visualization.
limitations: Requires the ete3 Python package and optional GUI dependencies for rendering features.
NCBITaxa may download a large local taxonomy database on first use.
Does not replace biological validation of phylogenetic assumptions or input data quality.
Large trees can require careful memory management and iterator-based workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare gene trees for analysis
use_cases.description: Convert, prune, root, and validate Newick trees before downstream phylogenetic workflows.

use_cases.title: Identify evolutionary events
use_cases.description: Use PhyloTree patterns to detect duplications, speciations, orthologs, and paralogs in gene families.

use_cases.title: Create publication figures
use_cases.description: Render styled trees with support values, clade colors, circular layouts, and vector output formats.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a tree file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to explain how I can load my Newick tree, count leaves, inspect node names, and save a cleaned copy.

prompt_templates.title: Build a taxonomy workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to design a workflow that maps these species names to taxids, builds a taxonomy tree, and annotates each leaf with lineage data.

prompt_templates.title: Find orthologs and paralogs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to analyze a PhyloTree gene tree, configure species parsing, detect duplication events, and extract ortholog groups.

prompt_templates.title: Create a publication visualization plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to create a reproducible visualization plan for a phylogenetic tree with clade colors, support labels, circular layout, and SVG output.

output_examples.input: Summarize this tree and prepare it for downstream analysis.
output_examples.output: Claude outlines loading the Newick file, counting leaves, checking branch support, midpoint rooting, pruning selected taxa, and saving a processed tree.

output_examples.input: I need an NCBI taxonomy tree for several mammal species.
output_examples.output: Claude describes translating species names to taxids, building the minimal topology, annotating nodes with ranks, and noting the first-run taxonomy cache.

output_examples.input: Help me make a publication-ready SVG tree.
output_examples.output: Claude recommends TreeStyle settings, node styling rules, support labels, vector output, and a quick validation step before final rendering.

best_practices: Use iterators for large trees to reduce memory use.
Preserve branch lengths when pruning trees for phylogenetic analysis.
Use vector formats such as SVG or PDF for publication figures.
anti_patterns: Do not run first-time NCBITaxa downloads without checking available disk space.
Do not treat taxonomy annotations as a substitute for curated biological metadata.
Do not install GUI or system packages with elevated privileges without user approval.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps Claude use ETE Toolkit for phylogenetic tree analysis, taxonomy workflows, and tree visualization.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes helper scripts for tree operations and quick visualization, plus documentation examples.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Some NCBITaxa workflows may download or update the NCBI taxonomy database on first use.

faq.question: Can it create publication figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents rendering trees to PDF, SVG, and PNG with custom styles and layouts.

faq.question: Can it detect orthologs?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides PhyloTree workflows for evolutionary events, ortholog groups, and paralog identification.

faq.question: What should users watch for?
faq.answer: Users should approve large taxonomy downloads and any sudo package installation before running related commands.
